purpose: Cysteamine bitartrate is used to treat a rare inherited disease called cystinosis, where a substance called cystine builds up and damages organs, especially the kidneys. It helps slow down kidney damage and other organ problems caused by this condition. It is a lifelong treatment that needs to be taken regularly to work well.
how_it_works: In cystinosis, cystine gets trapped inside cells and builds up to harmful levels. Cysteamine works by entering those cells and breaking down cystine into smaller pieces that can escape and be removed from the body. Think of it like a key that unlocks the buildup and lets the body clear it out.
common_side_effects: Nausea, vomiting, stomach upset, loss of appetite, and a strong body or breath odor are the most common side effects. Some people also experience diarrhea, tiredness, or fever. These side effects may lessen over time as your body adjusts to the medication.
warnings: Do not stop taking this medication without talking to your doctor, as stopping can cause serious harm to your kidneys and other organs. Tell your doctor if you notice skin rashes, bone pain, or sores around the mouth, as these may be signs of rare but serious side effects. This medicine should be taken exactly as prescribed — taking too little or skipping doses can make it much less effective.
typical_dosing: The dose is based on your body weight and is usually taken every 6 hours for regular capsules (Cystagon) or every 12 hours for the extended-release version (Procysbi). Your doctor will start you on a lower dose and slowly increase it to find the right amount for you. It is best taken with food to help reduce stomach upset.
